posts.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
posts.summary:
Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi EV delivered 31,267 units in July, marking its fourth consecutive month above 30,000 units but leaving the company at only 39% of its 550,000-unit annual target.
To meet its full-year goal, Xiaomi must significantly accelerate production to average nearly 67,000 units per month for the remainder of the year.

The company is pivoting toward the extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) segment with its new Sky Nomad series, aiming to compete directly with Li Auto and Huawei-backed Aito at aggressive price points.

posts.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
posts.summary:
112G PHY IP for linear optics to reduce power, latency and thermal load for high-speed data movement in AI and data center systems.
The post Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has introduced a 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, designed to enable DSP-less host-to-module connectivity.
Adopting linear optics can reduce module power consumption by up to 50% and significantly lower thermal loads, which is essential for scaling dense AI infrastructure.
By eliminating the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers, this technology provides a scalable path toward 224G/448G interconnects and Co-Packaged Optics (CPO).
The standardization of linear drive optics creates a repeatable, interoperable ecosystem, addressing a major bottleneck in high-speed data movement for AI data centers.

posts.title: 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec)
posts.summary:
Researchers from imec published a technical paper titled “Are Gate-All-Around 2D CFETs the Optimal Architecture for the A2 Node and Beyond?” Abstract Excerpt: “Here, we develop an A2-oriented 2D CFET integration flow with a CPP of 36 nm and Lg of 10 nm and present initial demonstrations of several key process modules. Despite their atomically... » read more
The post 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Imec researchers evaluated 2D Gate-All-Around (GAA) CFET architectures for the A2 node, utilizing a 36 nm contacted poly pitch (CPP) and 10 nm gate length.
The study concludes that 2D GAA CFETs do not currently offer a scaling advantage over silicon GAA CFETs at the A2 node due to similar contact formation constraints.
Successful implementation of these architectures requires rigorous co-optimization of contact resistance and parasitic extraction to realize potential PPA benefits.
The findings highlight the necessity of multiscale power-performance-area (PPA) evaluation frameworks to bridge the gap between theoretical channel advantages and practical fab integration.

posts.title: Defect Prediction in Optical Lithography, EUVL, and NIL (National Taiwan University)
posts.summary:
National Taiwan University researchers published a technical paper titled “From Lithography to Nanoimprint: Physics-Based, Data-Driven, and Hybrid Frameworks for Defect Prediction in Advanced Patterning Technologies.” Abstract: “Advanced patterning technologies have evolved from direct optical image transfer into predictive manufacturing frameworks in which defects are shaped by imaging physics, material response, process variation, and computational correction.... » read more
The post Defect Prediction in Optical Lithography, EUVL, and NIL (National Taiwan University) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: National Taiwan University researchers reviewed the evolution of defect prediction, noting that modern patterning technologies like EUVL and Nanoimprint Lithography (NIL) require new modeling paradigms beyond traditional optical correction.
EUVL introduces unique stochastic challenges such as photon-limited variability and mask 3D effects, while NIL shifts defect origins toward viscoelastic deformation and template interaction.
The paper advocates for hybrid frameworks that combine physics-based interpretability with data-driven machine learning to improve pattern recognition and uncertainty-aware screening.
This shift toward physically grounded, data-efficient prediction is critical for maintaining yield as advanced patterning moves away from simple geometry-driven correction logic.

posts.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
posts.summary: Business and technology leaders need no convincing that the time of agentic AI is here. Organizations are rapidly adopting agents, and few executives doubt the technology’s potential to transform work. But many organizations find that realizing the desired return on investment (ROI) from AI hinges on having the right foundation, with inadequate infrastructure and data…
bullets: Enterprise adoption of agentic AI is currently constrained by legacy data infrastructure, which limits the ability of agents to access the structured and unstructured data required for autonomous decision-making.
A survey of 300 executives reveals that AI agents currently have access to only 45% of total enterprise data on average, with 'data laggards' restricted to 30% or less.
Organizations identified as 'data leaders' provide agents with access to over 70% of their data, directly correlating with higher ROI and more successful deployment of autonomous systems.

With Gartner predicting that AI agents will automate or augment 50% of business decisions by 2027, firms must modernize data architectures to prevent operational bottlenecks and ensure agent reliability.
